"50X The Cash" has 119,556 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "50X The Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
981.headline: A close look at the prizes

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" has had no $1 million top prize claimed for close to two months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "MAX-A-MILLION" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 20.
985.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

988.body:
The most common win left on "Emerald 10's" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If you play "Emerald 10's" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
988.headline: What the prize table shows

990.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "LADY LUCK", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with two of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything here about "LADY LUCK" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 20.
990.headline: Where this game is in its run

992.body:
The prize money on "$2 MILLION VAULT" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over twelve prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $2 million. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

If "$2 MILLION VAULT" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
992.headline: Where the prize money is

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone four months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything here about "$5,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 20.
993.headline: Four months, no top prize claimed

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has one of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "$25,000 Triple Play" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
994.headline: Tickets sold so far

995.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$200,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

The numbers for "$200,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
995.headline: How much has sold

996.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has four of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
996.headline: No top prize claimed lately
